reviewer: historian_life_dates; independent targeted cross-check, not dossier owner
scope: Only Walker’s mediated Gramsci and Fanon proposals; actual named-reader argument, credits, identity and editions. No repeat of the full dossier or final coverage approval.
assessment: PASS within the proposals’ expressly mediated scope. Both sources specifically attribute Walker’s use, rather than merely mentioning thinkers alongside him. No required correction detected.

exact_locators: Printed p. 47, §2.2.3, final paragraph, explicitly begins Ranginui Walker’s (2002) title presents a clear view and then identifies his Gramsci citation.
Printed p. 48 opening continues the same paragraph’s account of one-sided media discourse and Walker’s insistence on radical mainstream-media changes.
Title/credit page, printed p. 1; copyright printed p. 3; bibliography printed p. 140, separate Ranginui 2002 and Tai 2004 entries; Appendix 1 p. 143 identifies the research team.
cases.short_primary_witness: He cites Gramsci on the double supremacy of the coloniser
cases.argument_check: The paragraph explicitly attributes the Gramsci citation to Ranginui Walker’s 2002 Māori news is bad news. It identifies domination plus intellectual/moral leadership, then explains monocultural media’s support for structural inequality and examples of one-sided coverage. The contribution claim is specifically supported.
cases.identity_guard: The report coauthor Tai Walker is distinct from Ranginui Walker. Crucially, the preceding paragraph’s Walker (2004) worldview citation belongs to Tai Walker’s Valuing Māori ways of knowing and being, as the bibliography confirms. The proposed Gramsci route correctly rests on the next paragraph’s explicitly named Ranginui Walker (2002), not on that adjacent Tai 2004 citation.
cases.work_guard: Bibliography p. 140 identifies Ranginui Walker, Māori news is bad news, in J. McGregor and M. Comrie, eds., What’s news? (Dunmore Press, 2002), pp. 215–232. This does not identify a particular Gramsci edition or page.
cases.reading_extent: Fresh selected text pp. 47–48 plus visual local publisher-PDF page images, full team/title credits, copyright and bibliography p. 140; public publisher PDF independently opened. Not the whole 185-page report.
cases.unread_limits: Walker’s 2002 original chapter and Gramsci’s original passage/edition remain unread; this is the named scholarly team’s report of his use, not a newly read direct Walker quotation.

exact_locators: Printed p. 8, second paragraph: colonial disavowal discussion explicitly identifies Ranginui Walker and other Māori historians following Fanon.
Note 48 begins at the foot of printed p. 13 and continues at the top of p. 14. It explicitly says Walker owes inspiration to Fanon and cites the revised 2004 book.
Printed p. 1 and running headings identify joint authors Giselle Byrnes and Catharine Coleborne; journal 45.1 (2011).
cases.short_primary_witness: Walker’s work owes its inspiration to that of Frantz Fanon
cases.argument_check: This is an explicit scholarly attribution, strengthened by the body’s named colonial-disavowal argument: colonial power itself enables resistance. It is more specific than juxtaposition or common postcolonial vocabulary. The note identifies Walker’s counter-narrative of colonization and named Fanon works.
cases.edition_guard: Note 48 cites Ranginui Walker, Ka Whawhai Tonu Mātou: Struggle Without End, revised edition, Auckland, 2004. It then cites Fanon, The Wretched of the Earth, London, 1965, and Black Skin, White Masks, London, 1968. These are the cited manifestations, not the originals’ first-publication dates. No evidence here licenses backdating the verified Fanon route to Walker’s 1990 first edition.
cases.reading_extent: Fresh selected publisher/institutional PDF text and actual page images of printed pp. 8, 13, 14; opening/title authorship also checked. Public institutional PDF independently opened. Not a whole-article or original-book reading.
cases.unread_limits: Walker’s 1990 and revised 2004 book bodies and cited Fanon editions remain unread. Retain the named-reader exception; no direct original-book verification, exclusive lineage or sole source of Māori historiography is claimed.

final_approval: Astra retains final passage/coverage approval and packet/input hashes.
raw_policy: No raw source passages copied into public assets; this report uses short witnesses and paraphrases only. Existing private page images/PDFs inspected read-only.
